1	title: 'feat(gauge): `progress.color` supports `''auto''`'
2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Gauge authors can already let some visuals inherit the series color automatically, but progress arcs still require manual color duplication, which makes themed gauges harder to maintain.
6	
7	  ## Desired outcome
8	
9	  Gauge progress should accept `progress.color: ''auto''` so the progress fill can follow the series color mapping automatically.
10	
11	  ## Acceptance signals
12	
13	  When `progress.color` is set to `''auto''`, the gauge progress arc adopts the expected automatic color instead of requiring an explicit hard-coded fill.
14	
15	  '

input.summary: Gauge progress arcs must honor the `'auto'` color keyword the same way the pointer already does: when `series.progress.itemStyle.color` (or a data item's `progress.itemStyle.color`) is `'auto'`, the progress sector's fill must be resolved from the axisLine color-stop mapping (`getColor`) at the item's normalized value, instead of staying the literal string `'auto'`. The fix is a small addition in `GaugeView._renderPointer`'s per-item styling loop; no new option keys, defaults, or type changes are required (`ProgressOption.itemStyle` is already `ItemStyleOption`, whose `color` accepts any string).
steps: No option-interface or default changes are needed. Confirm (do not edit) `ProgressOption` in src/chart/gauge/GaugeSeries.ts lines 73-80 — it already declares `itemStyle?: ItemStyleOption`, whose `color` is `ZRColor` (a string union), so `progress: { itemStyle: { color: 'auto' } }` compiles today; the published 6.1.0 `types/dist/echarts.d.ts` (lines 11687-11694) has the identical unchanged interface. Likewise `GaugeSeriesModel.defaultOption.progress` (GaugeSeries.ts lines 227-234: `show/overlap/width/roundCap/clip`) is unchanged in 6.1.0 — do NOT add a `color: 'auto'` default, since that would change the default rendering of every progress gauge.

Verification / test surface: there are no gauge unit tests under /workspace/test/ut/spec (only api, component, data, model, scale, series/{aria-columns-exclude,custom}, util). If you add one, create test/ut/spec/chart/gauge.test.ts following the pattern of test/ut/spec/series/custom.test.ts (`import { createChart } from '../../core/utHelper'`), set a gauge series with `axisLine: {lineStyle: {color: [[0.3, '#ff0000'], [1, '#00ff00']]}}`, `progress: {show: true, itemStyle: {color: 'auto'}}`, one data value, then read the rendered sector's `style.fill` (e.g. via `chart.getModel().getSeriesByIndex(0).getData().getItemGraphicEl(...)` is the pointer, so instead traverse the view group or assert via `(chart as any)._chartsMap` / zr storage) and expect the stop color, not `'auto'`. Cheaper manual check: add a fifth/sixth case to /workspace/test/gauge-progress.html mirroring `option5` (lines ~300-345) but with `axisLine.lineStyle.color` stops and `progress.itemStyle.color: 'auto'`, and confirm the arc is no longer rendered with the fallback/default fill.
input.risks: 1) Wording: the requirement title says `progress.color`, but there is no such option path in ECharts — the real option is `series-gauge.progress.itemStyle.color` (and the per-item `data[i].progress.itemStyle.color`, which is what `itemModel.getModel(['progress', 'itemStyle'])` reads). Do not invent a top-level `progress.color` key; upstream 6.1.0 did not add one. 2) `getColor` maps against `axisLine.lineStyle.color` stops; the default is a single stop `[[1, tokens.color.neutral10]]` (GaugeSeries.ts line 223), so with no custom stops `'auto'` resolves to the neutral gray, not the palette color — that is the same semantics the pointer already has and is expected. 3) `_renderTitleAndDetail` line 673-675 (`seriesModel.get(['progress', 'show']) ? data.getItemVisual(idx, 'style').fill : autoColor`) still derives the detail text color from the item visual fill, so a gauge using `progress.itemStyle.color: 'auto'` can have detail text colored differently from the arc; 6.1.0 left this untouched — do not "fix" it here. 4) Emphasis/blur states built by `setStatesStylesFromModel(progress, itemModel)` (line 568) do not resolve `'auto'` in `emphasis.itemStyle.color`; same pre-existing limitation as the pointer, out of scope. 5) Hoisting `autoColor` makes it computed even when only `showProgress`/`showPointer` is false-ish per branch; negligible, and matches upstream. 6) `data.get(valueDim, idx)` can be NaN for missing values; `linearMap(..., true)` clamps and `getColor` falls back to the first/last stop — same behavior as the existing pointer path.
